baselines_measured.torch_compile: REAL, measured; compile+specialization excluded from timed region (one untimed warmup call before the timed loop)
baselines_measured.flashinfer_native_fused: ATTEMPTED, NOT AVAILABLE on this GPU (sm_75 unsupported by installed flashinfer-python 0.6.12's rmsnorm kernel dispatch) -- honestly reported as unavailable, not fabricated
baselines_measured.vllm_own_rmsnorm_dispatch: PROFILED separately (not part of the 12-shape sweep): vllm.ir.ops.rms_norm emits 'Priority not set for op rms_norm, using native implementation' and dispatches to the SAME eager decomposition (aten::pow/mean/mul), confirming vLLM's own production RMSNorm path on this GPU/vLLM-version IS the eager baseline, not a separate fused kernel

custom_kernel_value_vs_fastest_non_custo.definition: custom_selected_median_ms vs min(eager_median_ms, torch_compile_median_ms) per shape
custom_kernel_value_vs_fastest_non_custo.conclusion: custom CUDA kernel beats torch.compile (the fastest real non-custom baseline) at all 12/12 tested shapes, 1.34x-2.98x

selector_value_vs_one_globally_fixed_blo.definition: one single block size (chosen by minimizing SUM of median latency across all 12 shapes) held fixed for every shape, vs the selector's per-shape adaptive choice
selector_value_vs_one_globally_fixed_blo.conclusion: NEGATIVE/NEUTRAL RESULT, reported honestly: on this 12-shape sweep, always using block_size=512 is competitive with, and on average marginally BETTER than (mean ratio 0.986, i.e. selector ~1.4% slower on average), the selector's per-shape adaptive choice. The selector wins clearly only at 1/12 shapes (128x1024, +7.1%); it loses by up to 6.6% at others. This is because RMSNorm block-size latency differences are within a few percent at almost every shape -- the absolute op cost is tiny and dominated by launch/memory overhead, not by tile-size-sensitive compute, so there is little headroom for a shape-aware selector to exploit on THIS operation/shape domain.

rmsnorm_conclusion_category: CUSTOM_KERNEL_CLEAR_WIN (custom-kernel value) combined with a documented selector-value caveat: the selector reproduces the measured winner 12/12 (proving SELECTION ACCURACY), but does not clearly outperform a single well-chosen fixed block size on THIS shape domain (selector VALUE is neutral-to-slightly-negative here). These are reported as two separate findings per the task's explicit instruction not to conflate them.
